newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians pray against Israeli land seizure.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians pray against Israeli land seizure.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinians held Friday prayers on land in the northern West Bank to protest against its confiscation for stone quarries to be developed by Israeli investors, witnesses said.
They said Israeli peace activists joined the Palestinians for the peaceful protest near the West Bank town of Tulkarm.
Israeli soldiers, who have scuffled with Palestinians twice this week during protests against the land seizure, stayed away.

"I am astonished at the Israeli government's complicity with Israeli businessmen to control Palestinian lands," Izz el-Deen al-Sharif, the Palestinian governor of Tulkarm, told the crowd during a rally after the prayers.
One Israeli peace activist told the crowd the Israeli action was "robbery" and said it jeopordised peace moves.
Israel handed over eight West Bank towns and some 400 villages to Palestinian rule under interim peace deals but kept control of rural areas, including the area where the quarries are located.
It is due to begin handing over other parts of the West Bank to the PLO starting on March 7.
Peter Lerner, spokesman for the Israeli military's Civil Administration occupation arm, said the land transfer to investors was carried out in accordance with legal procedures.
He said the land was declared state property in the 1980s and when plans to develop quarries were submitted in 1985, Palestinians filed objections to the Israeli High Court and lost the case.
Lerner said Israel was entitled to award land to private investors to develop industrial zones, be they Palestinians or Israelis.
